claims.text: A tabletop is a facilitated discussion that tests roles, responsibilities, plan steps, interdependencies, and coordination during a scenario. The FFIEC handbook says tabletops alone are likely insufficient to validate recovery capability; pair them with a technical restore or functional recovery test that verifies usable data and recovery objectives. (high confidence)

NIST recommends treating tests, training, and exercises as complementary parts of a program with scheduled events. Its contingency-planning guidance calls for periodic events and events after organizational or system changes, documenting results in an after-action report, and capturing corrective actions to update the plan. (high confidence)

A meaningful restore-verification drill restores a backup into a new or non-production target using the established recovery process, queries or retrieves restored data, checks that it is available, accessible, and uncorrupted and within the RPO, and measures elapsed recovery time against the RTO. (high confidence)

After each test, record its date, results, gaps, and remediation, then update recovery procedures after exercises or infrastructure changes. MongoDB's business continuity guidance calls for historical test results and plan updates; the FFIEC handbook calls for post-exercise actions and risk-based test methods. (high confidence)

A completed backup job or stored backup object does not establish usable recovery. AWS warns against assuming an existing backup is operational or meets RTO/RPO; MongoDB recommends manual restore tests; Percona's MongoDB Operator v1.23.0 guide says an object is restorable only after it reaches `ready` and recommends practising a restore. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-08)

MongoDB recommends practicing manual restores in non-production, verifying restored data integrity, recording actual recovery time against RTO, comparing data loss with RPO, and checking documented steps and dependencies such as networks and credentials. AWS guidance also recommends checking that restored data is available, accessible, uncorrupted, and queryable, then measuring recovery against RTO and RPO. (high confidence)

MongoDB Atlas business continuity guidance says to test the plan at least semi-annually and recommends quarterly testing. This is product-specific guidance, not a universal cadence. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A June 2026 MongoDB sharded-cluster demonstration checked that all node volumes belonged to the backup set, compared restored document counts against pre/post-snapshot baselines, and recorded total restore time. (low confidence)

NIST defines a tabletop exercise as discussion-based: participants walk through roles, responsibilities, coordination, and decisions without deploying equipment or other resources. A tabletop can review whether a recovery plan and its people are ready, but it does not demonstrate that a backup can be restored with intact data or within the RTO; those require a technical recovery test. (high confidence)

MongoDB Atlas's current business continuity guide recommends testing the plan at least semi-annually, with quarterly testing recommended. For manual disaster recovery tests, it advises practicing restores in non-production, comparing measured recovery time to the RTO, checking restored data integrity and dependencies such as networks and credentials, and keeping test dates, results, issues, and remediation records. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
